subject: OKR greenlight request: Q4 slate, playbook edits, and QBR dry-run scheduling
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: OKR greenlight request: Q4 slate, playbook edits, and QBR dry-run scheduling

Team —

Attached is the Q4 OKR playbook (Q4_okr_playbook_v1.pdf). This is the consolidated slate from product, eng, and go-to-market that we committed to in August. Before I push this to the exec deck and schedule the QBR dry-run next week I need two things:

1) Quick gate from you on the slate (do the objectives reflect the right priority tradeoffs?)
2) Any redline requests to the success metrics by EOD Tuesday.

I’ve highlighted three owner questions in the doc (pages 4–6) where we need numeric targets or guardrails. I also dropped a proposed dry-run agenda (QBR_dryrun_agenda.xlsx) in the Drive link below.

Proposed timeline: signoff by end of Tuesday (Oct 13) -> circulate exec packet Wed -> dry-run Thu morning. If we miss Tue we push the dry-run by a week, which delays the public OKR publish.

Notes: we should include a short plug for the new batching/quantization guidance from product in the ops slide — that’s a quick win for Dedicated customers.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cQ4OKRPlaybook

Thanks —
Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Q4_okr_playbook_v1.pdf (application/pdf, 1.1MB); QBR_dryrun_agenda.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 45KB)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: OKR greenlight request: Q4 slate, playbook edits, and QBR dry-run scheduling

Thanks Tessa — quick read through while on the flight. High level: the objectives look right, but a couple of metric asks before I greenlight.

- Obj 2 (Serving economics): can we split the cost-per-token target into two bands (hosted vs. dedicated)? Ops will need separate gates for Hosted API customers.
- Obj 3 (Reliability): the SLO target is ambitious; recommend we phrase it as a staged target (baseline -> stretch) so we can show runway in the exec packet.

I added inline comments on pages 4/5 of the playbook (Drive). Also flagged one dependency: the new autoscaler change hits on Nov 2; if that slips we should reflect it in rollout milestones.

I’m available for a quick 20-min sync this afternoon if helpful.

—Kim
Kimberly Park
VP, Customer Reliability & Ops
Redwood Inference

Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Renee Park <renee@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 12:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: OKR greenlight request: Q4 slate, playbook edits, and QBR dry-run scheduling

Appreciate the pull together, Tessa. I skimmed the playbook and have two clarifying asks before greenlight:

1) For the ML infra cost metric under Obj 1, confirm whether that includes model compilation/serving infra for both private and dedicated customers. If so, call that out and provide current baseline numbers.
2) For customer-facing reliability SLAs, I want a short note on fallback behaviors (we have fallback policies in the runtime — can we include a one-slide example of graceful degradation?).

Renee from Acme is copied — she’s volunteered to give a short customer-scene anecdote if we want a customer quote in the packet. Renee: if you’re open, a 1–2 sentence quote about reduced tail latency after our Dedicated migration would be perfect for the reliability slide.

If we can get answers to 1–2 above by EOD Tuesday I’ll sign off. Otherwise we should push the dry-run.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Product Strategy
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: OKR greenlight request: Q4 slate, playbook edits, and QBR dry-run scheduling

Thanks Markus — good calls. Quick replies inline: 

1) ML infra cost metric: yes, intended to include both Dedicated and Private (we should split hosted later). Baseline numbers: Dedicated pool token cost = $0.0018/token (Q3 avg), Private on-prem varies (see appendix A of playbook). I’ll add a small table to the playbook and call out that Dedicated/Private are included in the metric.

2) Fallback behavior slide: agreed — ops has a short example we can adapt (prefix cache + regional fallback). I’ll add it as slide 9.

Renee — thank you for offering to help. A 1–2 sentence quote would be great; if you can send it back by Tue noon we’ll include it in the exec packet.

I updated the Drive doc and attached the revised playbook (v1). We should be ready to greenlight pending the two metric clarifications above. If we get those by Tue EOD I’ll mark as green and send the exec packet Wed AM.

Proposed dry-run Thu 10/15 9:30–11:00 AM PT — calendar invite to follow.

—Tessa

Attachments: Q4_okr_playbook_v1.pdf (updated)
